$comment: 50.T50.11 — the ONE cross-language CF->agent fixture.
Two independent tables carry this binding: TS `AGENT_CF`
(S4-4p-anima/modules/dispatch-validate.ts) and Rust `cf_to_agent`
(Body/S/S0/epi-cli/src/agent/vak.rs). They agreed by luck, not by contract,
and nothing would have caught a one-sided edit.
Both sides read THIS file. Neither greps the other's source — the same
discipline `vak_address.parity.json` established in 50.T50.03. Add a binding
here to bind it in both languages at once.
Canon: [[S4-SPEC]] -> VAK dispatch; S4-ARCHITECTURE.md:178 (Moirai host CF).
The 7-fold constitutional roster. Membership in this map IS the roster:
an agent absent from it does not participate in the cf-binding contract.
Checked by BOTH languages.
Moirai are Aletheia subagents, NOT constitutional agents. Each inherits the
CF of the constitutional territory it dissects during the Night' rehearing
pass, keyed by its night position (moirai-dispatch.ts:104-106).
RATIFIED 50.T50.11 against canon, not against a skill: S4-ARCHITECTURE.md:178
reads 'klotho->Eros, lachesis->Anima, atropos->Sophia', and the originating
spec (Legacy/superpowers/plans/2026-05-22-vak-as-operational-substrate.md:1480)
reads 'CF (0/1/2) Eros for Klotho, CF (4.0/1-4.4/5) Anima for Lachesis,
CF (5/0) Sophia for Atropos per spec'. The code was already right; two skills
were not. See `skillNotation` below.
TS-only: Rust carries no Moirai table. The fixture still records the ratified
value so the skill check has one source to agree with.
The two divergences 50.T50.11 was asked to decide and land. A SKILL.md is
NOT canon, so in both cases canon/code won and the skill text was corrected —
and is now machine-checked so it cannot drift back silently.
`forbidden` entries are the pre-50.T50.11 spellings. A skill file matching one
is a regression, not a variant.

nous.reason: Nous' CF is the fourfold-zero ground written as (00/00), the same spelling the code has always carried. (0000) is a legacy alias — the S2 coordinate syntax already lists it as one (bimba-mcp/src/coordinates/syntax.ts LEGACY_CONTEXT_FRAME_ALIASES) — and carrying two spellings of one frame is how a reader learns to treat the notation as approximate.

lachesis.reason: Lachesis measures at P4', and P4' is the 4.x lemniscate frame, which is Anima's CF. (4.5/0) is Psyche's CF — a different position, not a different name for the same one.

$comment: A DIVERGENCE THAT IS PINNED, NOT FIXED. Rust `cf_to_agent` returns
`&'static str` and answers an unknown CF with "psyche"; TS `agentForCf`
returns `undefined`. So for a CF outside the roster the two languages
disagree: one fabricates an agent, the other says it does not know.
Narrowing the Rust signature to an Option is a public-surface change beyond
this tranche, so the behaviour is recorded here and asserted by both sides
instead of being silently tolerated. If the surface is ever narrowed, this
key is what tells you the test is expecting the old shape.
